questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design CRD-driven, tenant-isolated policy with a centralized control plane, plus edge behavior and end-to-end validation. Demonstrates practical trade-offs between in-memory state, policy freshness, and resilience.

## Key Concepts

- CNFPolicy CRD design and lifecycle
- Sidecar control-plane sync via mTLS
- Per-tenant, per-pathHash isolation and sliding window counters
- Failure handling: 3xx trips within 120s, 60s cooldown
- Status exposure and minimal end-to-end validation

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example.org/v1
kind: CNFPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-A-default
spec:
  tenantID: "tenant-A"
  pathHash: "/api/v1/resource"
  windowSeconds: 120
  tripCount: 3
  cooldownSeconds: 60
```

```yaml
status:
  tripActive: false
  lastTripAt: "2026-03-10T12:34:56Z"
  message: "OK"
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would clock skew and bursty traffic affect the sliding window accuracy?
- What metrics and alerting would you add to detect policy drift or control-plane unavailability?

Why This Is Asked

Tests practical design of a per-tenant feature flag system in a CNF gateway stack, focusing on CRD design, a lean central policy API, and a sidecar with token authentication and caching.

Key Concepts

- Kubernetes CRD for per-tenant feature flags
- Sidecar fetch with short lived token and 60s cache
- Default semantics and tenant isolation
- End-to-end test in a single namespace

Code Example

```yaml

apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featureflags.cnf.example.com
spec:
  group: cnf.example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              perTenantFlags:
                type: object
              defaultEnabled:
                type: boolean
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: featureflags
    singular: featureflag
    kind: FeatureFlag
    shortNames:
    - ff
```

- How would you audit tenant flag usage and prevent leakage across tenants?

## Why This Is Asked
Evaluates end-to-end provenance for ephemeral CNF pods under autoscaling, tenant isolation, and runtime policy.

- Cosign, SBOM (SPDX/CycloneDX), Rekor
- OPA/Kyverno, per-tenant KMS keys
- Kubernetes HPA, ephemeral pods

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Kyverno policy enforcing provenance presence on Deployments
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: assert-provenance
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Provenance (digest + SBOM) required"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            provenance/digest: ?
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test provenance during rapid scale-out events?
- How would you adapt the flow for edge/air-gapped deployments?

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:

data:

    function filter(tag, dt)

      end
      return dt
    end
